mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals stronger household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods of >2% YoY GDPC1 growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and inflation expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during periods of UNRATE < 4% for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during periods of INDPRO < 12-month MA for 6 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in the 10-year Treasury yield below 2% signals a shift toward risk-on sentiment, which boosts S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: monetary tightening with falling long-term yields
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods of rising FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL < 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and real housing starts (HOUST) signals strengthening household demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 AND HOUST both rise month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during periods of concurrent GDPC1 and HOUST increases (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in the unemployment rate above 6% and a decline in real personal income (PAYEMS) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during periods of UNRATE > 6% and PAYEMS declines (t-test p > 0.05).
